=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): alternate (leaves are attached singly at different nodes along the stem, alternating sides, visible in multiple angles)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): clustered (leaves are concentrated at the apex of the seedling, with the lower stem appearing bare)
B. Leaf Complexity
    3. Leaf complexity (simple / compound): simple (leaves consist of a single blade without distinct leaflets)
    4. Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): N/A
    5. Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): N/A
    6. Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): N/A
C. Leaf Morphology
    7. Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.)): toothed (margins exhibit distinct, sharp serrations, clearly visible in close-up views)
    8. Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): lanceolate (leaves are elongated with the widest point below the middle, tapering to a point)
    9. Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): acuminate (leaf tip tapers gradually to a slender point)
    10. Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): cuneate (leaf base tapers into the petiole)
    11. Venation type (pinnate / palmate / parallel): pinnate (a central midrib with secondary veins branching off)
    12. Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): prominent and clearly visible, arising from the midrib and curving towards the margin
    13. Leaf surface features (glabrous, shiny, dull, rugose): shiny (leaf surfaces reflect light, indicating a glossy texture)
    14. Leaf surface trichomes (present / absent): absent (surfaces appear smooth without visible hairs)
    15. Petiole length (short / long): short (petioles are clearly present but relatively short compared to the leaf blade length)
    16. Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): terete (petioles appear round in cross-section, not flattened or winged)
D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17. Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): woody (stem appears stiff, dark, and lignified, characteristic of a tree seedling)
    18. Stem trichomes (present / absent): absent (stem appears smooth and hairless)
    19. Stem color: reddish-brown (stem exhibits a distinct reddish or rust-brown pigmentation)
    20. Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): smooth (stem surface appears relatively uniform without obvious ridges or large lenticels)
E. Other Visible Seedling Traits
    21. Stipules, sometimes visible only in close-up images (present / absent): absent (no stipules are clearly visible at the leaf nodes)
    22. Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed
    23. Pulvinus, for Fabaceae family only (present / absent): absent
    24. Tendrils (present / absent): absent
F. Notes: The seedling displays distinct serration on the leaf margins and a reddish-brown stem color. Some leaves show minor physical damage (small holes/margin missing), likely mechanical or abiotic, but no insects or pathogens are visible.
